name: Image charge
description: A large grounded sphere. Whatever charge you place near it, the metal answers with an opposite image charge inside: near the surface your charge is almost cancelled, far away the pair acts like a dipole. Steer the beam around the sphere.

reality.represents: Image charges: a grounded metal sphere

remarks.detail: For a sphere the method of images is exact: a charge q at distance d from a grounded sphere of radius a acts with the image −qa/d at a²/d from its centre.
A metal rearranges its charge within femtoseconds, instantly for a beam.
The particle's charge also induces an image that pulls it towards the metal; for its tiny charge this matters only within a hair of the surface, and it is left out.

Everything is symmetric about the plane z = 0, so the particle never leaves it. A real beam also has a width across the plane, where the same fields act differently (focusing in the plane can defocus across it).
